title: Kamarupa after the Palas

kamauli.title: Venis, Kamauli grant, EI II pp.347–358
kamauli.note: Regnal year 4; CE conversions include 1123 and 1142. Original editor favoured 1142; appointment sequence firmer than absolute chronology.

vallabha.title: Kielhorn, Assam plates of Vallabhadeva, EI V pp.181–188
vallabha.note: Saka 1107, conventionally 1185; editor allows 1184/1185. Genealogy is not a dated reign list; father gives the command for the donation.

kanai.title: IGNCA, Assam Rock Art Report 2015, Kanai Barasi
kanai.note: 1206 inscription locality; no securely named defender in the inscription.

bakhtiyar.title: Banglapedia, Bakhtiyar Khalji
bakhtiyar.note: Disastrous Tibet expedition and return in 1206; no exact local battle route inferred.

iwaz.title: Banglapedia, Iwaz Khalji
iwaz.note: Campaign and tribute context; Iwaz ruled 1212–1227, so do not date his death to 1228.

gachtal.title: Assam Directorate of Archaeology, Gachtal site
gachtal.note: Official inventory confirms a 13th-century inscription; precise 1227 reading and Visvasundara identification taken from scholarship, not independently re-collated.

gachtal-study.title: Madan-Kamdev historical study, chapter 2 p.50
gachtal-study.note: Discusses Gachtal Saka 1149/1227, Visvasundara, restoration and proposed Prithu identification.

ambari-location.title: ASI Guwahati Circle, Ambari excavation
ambari-location.note: Official coordinates 26°11′8″N,91°45′21″E; archaeological locality, not the located Yogihati establishment.

ambari-date.title: Anima Dutta, Political Geography of Pragjyotisa-Kamarupa p.143
ambari-date.note: Ambari inscription, Saka 1154/1232, Samudrapala. A Pala-suffix does not prove descent from Jayapala.

prithu.title: N.K. Bhattasali, New Lights on the History of Assam (1946)
prithu.note: Prithu identification debated; consulted catalogue summary and contrasted scholarship; full primary text not freshly collated.

sandhya.title: N.N. Acharyya, History of Medieval Assam (1966)
sandhya.note: Medieval transition context; compare Sarkar 1992 pp.39–41: Sandhya c.1250–1270, capital move not exactly dated.

sandhya-dating.title: North Bengal University historical-geography thesis, chapter 1
sandhya-dating.note: Discusses the capital shift around 1260; older campaign dates differ. Do not make 1257 the certain moving day.

rajpat.title: ASI Kolkata, Rajpat excavation report, Site Location
rajpat.note: Rajpat at 26°09′N,89°21′12″E. Archaeological identification does not date Sandhya’s move.

kanai-gps.title: Ancient Asia 15 (2024), petroglyph locality table
kanai-gps.note: Kanai Boroshi Bowa 26°12′36.5″N,91°44′31.4″E. Rock-art site coordinate; not exact battle location.

episodes.title: Pala succession and Bengal intervention
episodes.text: The end of the local Pala line and the extent of Bengal intervention are unsettled. Tingyadeva appears in the later Kamauli account as the ruler whose disaffection prompted replacement. Do not treat c.1110–1126 as dated epigraphic reign bounds.

episodes.date: First half of 12th century; regnal year 4
episodes.title: Vaidyadeva’s appointment and grant
episodes.who: Vaidyadeva, appointed by Kumarapala of Bengal
episodes.text: Kamauli records his replacement of Tingyadeva and a grant from Hamsakonci. It locates Kamarupa-mandala within Pragjyotisa-bhukti. Absolute dating is disputed:1123 and 1142 occur in scholarship. Hamsakonci is unlocated here; Kamauli near Varanasi is the discovery place, not his Assam capital.

episodes.title: Rulers known through Vallabhadeva’s genealogy
episodes.text: This is an ancestral sequence in a later record, not proof of three consecutively dated reigns across all Kamarupa. Relations to Vaidyadeva and the exact extent of their domains remain uncertain.

episodes.title: Vallabhadeva’s charitable endowment
episodes.text: The Assam plates record a food-distribution establishment near a Siva temple east of Kirtipur in Hapyacha-mandala, endowed at his father’s command. The editor permits 1184/1185. These places are not securely identified; a Tezpur find region is not a kingdom boundary.

episodes.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji’s failed expedition and return
episodes.who: Unnamed Kamarupa ruler(s); Prithu identification disputed
episodes.text: The Tibet expedition ended in a disastrous retreat. Kanai-Barashi-Bowa commemorates destruction of the invading Turks but does not name the defender. Prithu/Britu in Persian narratives has disputed identification, including an Awadh interpretation; no 1187–1228 reign or Bhitargarh capital is treated as established.

episodes.title: Iwaz’s pressure and the Gachtal evidence
episodes.who: Visvasundaradeva attested in scholarship; unnamed regional rulers
episodes.text: Iwaz’s eastern campaigns and tribute claims belong to this context. Gachtal’s stone record is read as Saka 1149/1227 and associated with Visvasundara and temple repairs. Equating him with Prithu is disputed. Iwaz’s death is conventionally 1227, not 1228. Succession and any brief Delhi-imposed tributary arrangement remain uncertain.

episodes.title: Samudrapala at Ambari
episodes.text: The Ambari inscription supplies a 1232 attestation, not a c.1100 reign. It mentions a royal-associated sattra at Yogihati. The king’s genealogy, accession, end of reign and full territory are not established. This display window is not an 18-year reign.

episodes.title: Sandhya and the western reorganisation
episodes.who: Sandhya, conventionally the Rai of Kamrup
episodes.text: Historians associate Sandhya with Kamarupanagara and the transition to Kamata. His accession and earlier genealogy are uncertain; do not extend his reign backward to 1229 as a settled fact.

episodes.title: Yuzbak defeated; transition toward Kamata
episodes.text: Yuzbak’s 1257 invasion ended in defeat and death during the retreat. The victory is attributed to Sandhya in the historical reconstruction. The move from Kamarupanagara to Kamatapur is usually placed after this, around 1260; it is not a securely dated same-day consequence.

spots.name: Kamarupanagara · North Guwahati
spots.note: Traditional regional identification. Exact medieval palace and urban perimeter are not established.

spots.name: Tezpur · Vallabhadeva plates
spots.note: General Tezpur reference, not an exact findspot or proven capital. Kirtipur and Hapyacha of the charter remain unlocated.

spots.name: Kanai-Barashi-Bowa · 1206
spots.note: Contemporary commemoration of the destruction of invading Turks. The rock does not name Prithu; its location does not identify the precise battlefield.

spots.name: Gachtal · c.1227
spots.note: Catalogue reference coordinate near Dabaka. Visvasundara and temple repair are discussed in scholarship; identification with Prithu is disputed. This is a stone record, distinct from Gopala’s earlier copper plates.

spots.name: Ambari · Samudrapala, 1232
spots.note: Saka 1154/1232 attestation of Samudrapala. The royal-linked Yogihati sattra mentioned in the record is not securely located here; this is not a modern Sankaradeva sattra.

spots.name: Kamatapur · Gosanimari/Rajpat
spots.note: ASI locality coordinate. Capital shift is associated with Sandhya, probably after 1257 and around 1260; exact year unknown. Existing border switch at 1257 is a display convention.

unlocated: Hamsakonci: Vaidyadeva’s issuing headquarters; exact site not established.
Kirtipur / Hapyacha-mandala: Vallabhadeva’s endowment locality; exact site not established.
Bhitargarh: do not show as Prithu’s certain capital.
